# Running a Standard City Scan

A standard City Scan runs the full default task suite for a single city. This is the most common use case.

## When to Use a Standard Scan

Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. Use a standard scan when:

- You have a clearly defined city boundary
- You want the complete default set of ~15 data layers
- You are producing a one-time deliverable for a single city

## Configuration

```yaml
# config.yml — standard scan
city: "Nairobi"
country: "KE"
aoi: "inputs/AOI/nairobi.geojson"
output_dir: "outputs/nairobi"
scan_type: standard
year: 2024
```

Sed do eiusmod tempor incididunt ut labore et dolore magna aliqua. No additional configuration is required for a standard scan — all default tasks will run automatically.

## Running the Scan

```bash
python run.py --config config.yml
```

Expected runtime for a typical city (~500 km²):

| Task Group | Estimated Duration |
|---|---|
| Population | 2–5 min |
| Land use & environment | 10–20 min |
| Infrastructure | 5–10 min |
| Risk & hazard | 15–30 min |
| **Total** | **~1 hour** |

: Estimated runtimes for a standard scan {#tbl-runtime}

## Default Task List

```python
DEFAULT_TASKS = [
    "population", "population_density",
    "landuse", "ndvi", "ndwi", "urban_heat",
    "roads", "buildings", "accessibility",
    "flood_risk", "coastal_erosion", "seismic",
]
```
